title: Programming fundamentals (CS1)
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to program systematically in Python: expressions and types, branching and iteration, functions and specifications, strings, tuples, lists and dictionaries, mutability and aliasing, recursion, testing, debugging and exceptions, classes and inheritance, and an introduction to algorithmic complexity, searching and sorting.
primary_reading: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.100L: Introduction to CS and Programming Using Python

blocks.deliverable: Write programs with loops and conditions, and trace them by hand.
Implement bisection search for a square root.
Write functions that transform nested data.
Week 7 midterm; write recursive functions with tests.
Design a class hierarchy for a simple domain.
Analyze the running time of five functions.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: A complete program from a specification: for example a word game, a text-based data analyzer or a simulation; 300–500 lines with a written design, unit tests for every function, and a short report on the running time of its key parts.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
